title: dngn.io: AI DM daily dungeon game (with a twist)
author: Necessary_Pseudonym
selftext:
Hey all, happy Halloween!

I helped create dngn.io: a free-to-play web-based daily dungeon text adventure that is led by an AI DM. Each day a new "room" is generated (via Opus 5.5). The rooms are essentially puzzles to be solved / eecape-room type. The user gets 3 items to potentially use, and can do literally any action. The outcome is guided by a dice-roll and DM intuition. The more "flaire" the better the chance it succeeds. 

The interesting addition to the game is that we allowed the AI DM to learn from user inputs throughout the day. So the daily room changes periodically throughout the day. This limits overused approaches to the puzzle, and forces players to think uniquely.

The twist here is that we ultimately aim to train an internal model with input data. The model will focus on piloting the entire game. By using user inputs to train the model, it will learn deeply how people interact with the open-ended world, and be able to optimize the experience over time. We already use player data to update the game throughout the day (as mentioned) and make/judge new rules for the DM to consider.

Let me know what you think! While we are in Beta, the current game uses Claude APIs. Has anyone been able to come up with creative ways to reduce cost for api-use while still keeping good and consistent outputs? For responses, dngn.io currently employs Haiku with Sonnet escalations, which works marginally better than just Haiku.
